title: Over 50 Iterations: How Incolor Designs Their Bikes

takeaways.text: Incolor's engineer says SR and SR+ are the same model and mould with different lay-ups (T800 versus T1100), about 60 g apart, with the same comfort and build quality; the SR+ adds 3D-printed titanium parts.
He says the SR's CFD work took two to three months, the SSR's about six months, and a full new frame about a year from design to production.
The Voyager gravel/all-road frame, he says, shares the SR's design language with 45 mm tire clearance and takes a front derailleur; a longer, wider-clearance gravel model may follow.

disclosure: Expo interview with Incolor's frame engineer; the answers are the manufacturer's own statements, not independent tests.
summary: Interview with Incolor's frame engineer covering the Speedster SR/SR+, Voyager, SSR and TTR concept; the opening section explains how SR and SR+ differ.
